# Configurable hover-intent delay for the shared TooltipManager — intake brief

**Headline:** The shared `TooltipManager` gains a configurable delay before a tooltip
appears — a mouse-hover dwell and a separate (shorter) touch press-and-hold dwell — with
a default of 0 ms so every existing game's behaviour is unchanged. The Rising opts in
with 1500 ms hover / 500 ms touch to stop tooltips flashing as the pointer sweeps a busy
board.

> **Provenance:** created as the core-engine half of `RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH` ("Delay
> tooltips by 1.5") on the producer's instruction to put the capability in the engine and
> make the game item depend on it. Producer answers (2026-11-19): scope = core-engine
> capability opted into by the game (Q1c); touch = a shorter touch delay of ~500 ms
> (Q2c); the game's hover-raise stays immediate, only the overlay is delayed (Q3a).

## Problem statement

`TooltipManager.show()` renders its overlay the moment a caller invokes it, so a host
game that shows tooltips on `pointerover` (or on the scene pointer entering a card face)
flashes tooltip text for every target the pointer merely passes over. Hosts cannot ask
for a dwell period: there is no delay, no timer and no cancellation in the manager, so
each game would otherwise have to re-implement "hover intent" itself — with its own
timer lifecycle bugs (un-cleared timers, stale anchors, shows after dismissal).

## Users

- **Game developers (host scenes).** Want a supported, tested way to require a dwell
  before a tooltip appears, and a way to opt in with two numbers (hover, touch) instead
  of writing their own timer plumbing.
- **Players.** Should not see overlay text flash while sweeping the pointer across
  interactive targets; should still see a tooltip when they deliberately dwell (mouse)
  or press and hold (touch).
- **Maintainers.** Want one engine-owned timing rule with tests, rather than per-game
  variants that drift.

## Desired behaviour

- `TooltipManager` accepts a **hover delay** and a **touch delay** through its
  constructor config, both defaulting to **0 ms** — an existing caller that passes no
  timing config keeps today's immediate behaviour exactly.
- With a non-zero delay, `show()` **schedules** the overlay: nothing is rendered before
  the delay elapses, and the overlay appears once it does.
- The caller tells the manager which delay applies (mouse hover vs touch
  press-and-hold); the mechanism must be explicit and deterministic (e.g. an
  `inputType`/`source` argument on `show()`, or an equivalent documented contract), not
  inferred unreliably from global pointer state.
- A repeated `show()` **while a show is pending** refreshes the pending content and the
  anchor coordinates (so the overlay lands at the live pointer) but **does not restart
  the delay** — continuous pointer movement within the same target must not postpone the
  tooltip forever.
- `hide()` and `destroy()` cancel any pending show; no tooltip may appear after either,
  and no timer may be left behind (no leak across scene teardown).
- The Settings "Tooltips" suppression still wins: with tooltips off, a scheduled show
  never appears.
- Delay `0` on both paths must reproduce today's behaviour byte-for-byte (immediate
  render, same position, same Phaser/DOM modes).
- The delay must be testable without real-time sleeps (an injectable clock / Phaser
  `time` timer that tests can advance, plus a guard for scenes without a time manager).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `TooltipManager` exposes configurable `delayMs` and `touchDelayMs` (names illustrative) on its constructor config, both defaulting to 0, and existing callers that pass no timing config behave exactly as before (immediate show, unchanged DOM and Phaser rendering).
- With a non-zero hover delay, `show()` does not render the overlay before the delay elapses and renders it once the delay has elapsed.
- The touch press-and-hold path can use a different (shorter) delay than mouse hover, selected explicitly by the caller.
- A repeated `show()` while a show is pending updates the pending content and anchor coordinates without restarting the delay; the overlay appears at the most recent anchor when it fires.
- `hide()` cancels a pending show, and `destroy()` cancels and clears it — no overlay appears after either call, and no timer survives teardown.
- With `SettingsPanel.showTooltips === false` a scheduled show never appears, and the suppression check still short-circuits as today.
- Unit tests in `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` cover: delay 0 = immediate; no show before the delay; show after the delay; no delay restart on repeated `show()`; pending-show cancellation via `hide()` and `destroy()`; touch delay distinct from hover delay; suppression with a pending show.
- Browser tests in `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` cover the delayed show against a real Phaser scene (advanced clock, no real-time sleeps), including the Phaser-render mode.
- The Gym tooltip demo (`example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts`) exercises a non-zero delay so the behaviour can be verified manually.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (TooltipManager / `attachHudTooltipZone` sections) documents the delay options, the default-0 backwards compatibility and the pending-show semantics; any Gym index entry for the demo scene is updated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Any game built on the engine can require a deliberate dwell before a tooltip appears —
one config pair instead of hand-rolled timers — while games that do not opt in keep
today's instant tooltips, so hovering across a busy board no longer flashes overlay text.

## Constraints

- **Backwards compatibility is the hard constraint:** delay `0`/absent must be
  indistinguishable from today for every existing caller (The Rising, the Gym demo, and
  `attachHudTooltipZone`'s hover/tap handlers).
- **No new host-side plumbing:** the timer, cancellation and stale-anchor handling live
  in the manager, not in each game.
- **Phaser and DOM modes both honoured** (the manager has two render paths; the delay
  gates both).
- **No real-time sleeps in tests** — the engine suite runs in CI; a fakeable clock or
  Phaser timer path is required.
- **Do not change tooltip placement, wrapping or content composition** — only *when* the
  overlay first appears.
- **Do not add a user-facing setting** for the delay; it is a host-game configuration
  value. The existing Tooltips on/off toggle is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManagerConfig` (line 87) has a single optional
  `phaserRender` callback; the class (line 207) owns the DOM node and the Phaser
  container. `show(content, x, y, ctx)` (line 262) renders immediately (destroying and
  recreating the Phaser container, or setting the DOM node's text/position/display);
  `hide()` (line 356) destroys the container and hides the node; `destroy()` (line 372)
  cleans both up. There is **no** timer, delay or pending state anywhere.
- `src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `attachHudTooltipZone(...)` (line 299) wires
  `pointerover` → `tooltipManager.show(...)`, `pointerout` → `hide()`, and an optional
  tap toggle; it inherits whatever timing the manager provides.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — creates both a DOM manager (line 169)
  and a Phaser-mode manager (line 171) and shows tooltips from demo triggers
  (lines ~285–305); the natural place to demo a delay.
- Established engine precedent for timers: `src/ui/HighlightManager.ts` uses
  `scene.time.delayedCall`, and `src/ui/illegalMoveToastView.ts` guards
  `time?.delayedCall` so scenes (and unit-test mocks) without a time manager still work.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (constructor/DOM/positioning/suppression),
  `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (real Phaser scene),
  `tests/ui/SettingsPanelTooltips.browser.test.ts` (toggle), and the Gym tooltip specs.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager` and the tooltip zone helper;
  `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps gym scenes to APIs.

## Desired change

Add an opt-in hover-intent delay to the shared `TooltipManager`: two configurable
durations (mouse hover, touch press-and-hold, both default 0), a cancellable pending-show
state that refreshes its content/anchor without restarting the timer, clean cancellation
on `hide()`/`destroy()`, correct interaction with the Settings suppression, and tests that
advance a fakeable clock rather than sleeping. Demo the capability in the Gym tooltip
scene and document it.

## Plan

**Decision:** no child items. This is a single vertical slice — one engine module
(`src/ui/Tooltip.ts`) plus its unit/browser specs, the Gym demo and docs. Effort
`Small` (≈9.6 h expected) with every AC landing in the same file, so decomposing it
into features would add coordination overhead without producing any independently
deliverable increment. The effort/risk pre-check returned `plan` only because risk is
`Medium` (the skip threshold requires `Low`); the agent evaluation in Process step 1
concludes the brief is already actionable (measurable ACs + implementation sketch +
Key Files), so planning completes with review rather than decomposition.

### Locked contract (adjustable at implement time, but state the final choice)

- `TooltipManagerConfig` gains `delayMs?: number` (mouse hover) and `touchDelayMs?: number`
  (touch press-and-hold), both defaulting to `0`.
- `show(content, x, y, ctx?, inputType?: 'hover' | 'touch' = 'hover')` — the delay source
  is an explicit trailing argument, so every existing 1–4 argument call site keeps its
  current signature and its immediate behaviour.
- `0` (or an absent config) renders synchronously on the existing code path — no timer is
  ever scheduled, preserving frame timing for every current caller.
- A non-zero delay schedules exactly one pending show (`{ content, x, y, ctx, inputType }`
  plus a `Phaser.Time.TimerEvent` from a guarded `this.scene?.time?.delayedCall`). A
  repeated `show()` while pending overwrites the pending content/anchor/ctx and leaves the
  timer running (no restart). A repeat for a different target inside the window reuses the
  elapsed dwell — documented behaviour, and `pointerout` → `hide()` cancels in practice.
- `hide()` / `destroy()` cancel the pending timer (`remove(false)`) and clear the pending
  state. The Settings suppression check stays at the top of `show()` and is re-checked
  when the timer fires (defence in depth).
- No time manager (bare unit-test mocks / headless) → render immediately, mirroring the
  guarded `time?.delayedCall` precedent in `src/ui/illegalMoveToastView.ts`.

### Implementation order (test-first)

1. `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — new specs (delay 0 immediate; nothing rendered
   before the delay; renders after it; no restart on a repeated show; `hide()` and
   `destroy()` cancellation; touch delay distinct from hover; suppression with a pending
   show) driven by a fake `scene.time.delayedCall` the test controls. → verify: the new
   specs fail before the implementation exists.
2. `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — config fields, pending state, timer wiring, cancellation, both
   render modes gated by the same pending show. → verify: unit specs green and the
   existing specs unchanged.
3. `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — real Phaser scene with the clock advanced
   (no real-time sleeps), covering DOM and Phaser render modes. → verify: `--project
   browser` green.
4. `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — opt both managers into a non-zero demo
   delay and reflect the timing in the event log / help text.
5. `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Tooltip Manager + § `attachHudTooltipZone` — document
   `delayMs`/`touchDelayMs`, default-0 backwards compatibility, the pending-show and
   anchor-refresh semantics and the no-time-manager fallback; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` —
   note the demo's delay capability. `src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` JSDoc gains the
   pass-through note.

### Handling of the "all related documentation" AC

`README.md` carries no tooltip documentation today (verified: zero matches for
"tooltip"), so the related documentation surface is `docs/DEVELOPER.md`,
`docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` and the `attachHudTooltipZone` JSDoc. The implementer records
that check rather than editing `README.md` for its own sake.

### Open design points closed by this plan

- **Caller-selected delay:** explicit `inputType` argument on `show()` (not inference
  from global pointer state).
- **Gym demo:** a fixed non-zero demo delay, no new slider (slider would be scope creep
  and a UI change beyond "when the overlay appears").

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-19 — plan skill: no child items created (single-slice capability); locked the
  `delayMs`/`touchDelayMs` + `inputType` contract, the test-first implementation order and
  the doc targets; six automated review stages run, no AC changes required; existing
  effort/risk estimate (`Small` / `Medium`, 9.58 h expected) re-confirmed as current.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — the manager: config interface, pending-show state, timer wiring,
  cancellation in `hide()`/`destroy()`, both render paths.
- `src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `attachHudTooltipZone` (hover/tap trigger) — pass through
  the delay/source so the helper keeps working unchanged for callers that do not opt in.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — unit specs for the delay gate and cancellation.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — real-scene specs with an advanced clock.
- `tests/ui/SettingsPanelTooltips.browser.test.ts` — suppression with a pending show.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — demo a non-zero delay.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — document the delay options and default-0 compatibility.
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` — note the demo scene's delay capability.

## Cross-repo dependency

- **Blocks `RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH`** ("Delay tooltips by 1.5", The Rising). That game item
  hosts the opted-in call with `delayMs = 1500` (mouse) and `touchDelayMs = 500`
  (press-and-hold) and keeps its covered-card hover-raise immediate, delaying only the
  overlay. The game change lands in the `tce-the-rising` store and consumes this
  capability through the `core` submodule, so this item must reach `dev` before the game
  side can ship.

## Related work

- `CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44` — Standardize TooltipManager across all games + create gym scene
  (introduced the single shared manager and both render modes).
- `CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7` — Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (the immediate
  hover show this item makes optional).
- `CG-0MT24RFIV007NQMP` — Tooltips for business cards do not work reliably (host-side
  reliability history).
- `CG-0MQK4X80F004MQA6` — Tooltips for buttons should still display even when disabled.
- `CG-0MP1MPRF5000KB49` — Tooltip on played cards in Sushi Go.
- `CG-0MM1OPSGM052NPUN` — Magic numbers in scene layout and animation timing (timing
  constants convention).

Related docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (TooltipManager, tooltip zone helper),
`docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` (gym scene map), `docs/ui/ADAPTER-GUIDE.md`.

**Duplicate-work check performed** (`wl search "tooltip delay"`, `"hover delay"`,
`"hover intent"` in this store): no open or completed item adds a delay/hover-intent gate
to the manager; the tooltip history above is the feature this item extends.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Backwards compatibility.** Every existing caller passes no timing config; the default
  must be 0 ms and the code path must not schedule a timer at all (a scheduled 0 ms show
  would change frame timing). Mitigation: an explicit "no delay → render now" branch,
  covered by a spec.
- **Timer lifecycle.** A pending show is the new stateful thing: it must be cleared on
  `hide()`, `destroy()`, suppression, and scene shutdown, or a tooltip can appear after
  its trigger has gone (the classic stale-timer bug). Mitigation: cancellation specs plus
  a guard for a missing time manager.
- **Touch/hover selection.** Deciding the delay from global pointer state alone is
  fragile in mixed-input scenes; the item requires an explicit, testable signal from the
  caller.
- **Anchor freshness.** A 1.5 s wait makes a stale anchor visible; the pending show must
  track the latest coordinates.
- **Test-speed risk.** Real 1.5 s sleeps in CI are unacceptable; the fakeable clock is a
  requirement, not a nice-to-have.
- **Scope-creep guard.** User-configurable delays, tooltip "warm" fast paths (instant
  show on a neighbouring target once one is visible), and per-tooltip delay overrides are
  **not** in scope; they can be follow-up items.

### Assumptions (documented, adjustable)

- Both delays are absolute durations in milliseconds; 0 means "show immediately".
- The manager keeps a single pending show (its existing contract is one overlay at a
  time), so a new `show()` for a different target cancels and re-schedules rather than
  queueing.
- The delay is host configuration, not a player setting.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which side of the engine/game boundary should the delay live on?" — Answer
  (producer, 2026-11-19, via `RISE-0MWNEACUU009KOTH`): "Create a work item in the core
  engine and make this one dependent upon it" (option C = configurable delay on the
  manager, opted into by The Rising). Source: interactive reply on the game work item.
- Q: "Should touch press-and-hold use the same delay?" — Answer (producer, same reply):
  option C = a shorter touch delay (~500 ms). Source: interactive reply.
- Research performed: inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (no timing layer; two render paths),
  `src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` (`attachHudTooltipZone` hover/tap wiring),
  `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` (both managers, demo triggers),
  `src/ui/HighlightManager.ts` / `src/ui/illegalMoveToastView.ts` (engine timer
  precedent), and the existing tooltip specs in `tests/ui/`.

# Intake brief — Long Erasure: make the goodwill-gated branch survivable

## Problem statement

The one branch the scene help panel advertises as *earned* — `Sabotage the Loom`
(`cost=goodwill:3` on `le-ii-bargain`, leading to `le-ii-sabotage`) — is reachable
but **unwinnable**: every route that enters it arrives with exactly 2 clock while
every successor from that beat costs 3, so the run expires and the player who did
the most to earn the secret path is the only one who cannot finish the story.

## Users

- As a player who earned the secret branch (by transmitting the warning and
  sharing the berth), I want to reach the Loom's core and an ending, so that the
  state-gated reward is a reward rather than a trap.
- As a producer reviewing the Gym demonstrator, I want the help panel's promise
  ("the gated branch shows up when your journey has earned it") to describe what
  the balance actually delivers, so the showcase does not teach a falsehood.
- As an author, I want the route-space harness to be the arbiter of branch
  balance, so a future content edit cannot quietly make a branch unwinnable again.

## Existing state (measured, reproducible)

From `docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md` §4.4 (`CG-0MWNHZEGJ0099JFM`) and
re-measured for this intake with the committed harness:

```
npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts --seeds 5
playable routes=132 outcome={"reset":38,"closed":80,"expired":14}
gated beat: routes=4 completed=0 clockLeftOnEntry={"min":2,"max":2}
```

- The gated route (`Log the erasure → Transmit the warning → Shelter in the dead
  zone → Strip the derelict → Share the berth → Bargain in bad faith → Sabotage
  the Loom → …`) consumes **15 of the 17 clock** before leaving `le-ii-sabotage`:
  `le-i-open 1 + le-i-log 1 + le-i-transmit 2 + le-ii-shelter 2 + le-ii-salvage 2
  + le-ii-offer 2 + le-ii-bargain 3 + le-ii-sabotage 2`, then both successors
  (`le-iii-approach`, `le-iii-ahead`) cost 3.
- The goodwill path is structurally the *slow* path: it is the only path that both
  transmits the warning (+2 goodwill) and shares the berth (+1 goodwill), and
  `le-ii-bargain` (3 clock) is the most expensive non-Act-III beat in the content.
- 10 of the 14 expiring routes are on the bargain branch at all (the four sabotage
  routes plus six "Keep the bargain → Follow the thread" routes that consume
  18 clock), so the bargain branch is the clock's dominant victim.
- The gate itself works (option absent at goodwill 2, present at 3; the
  `#when=charge>=2` conditional successor fires) — this is a **content-balance
  defect, not an engine defect**.
- The scene help panel's "Pressure clock and state gates" slide and its Test Plan
  step 2 both promote the branch as an earned reward, which the balance does not
  deliver.

## Desired change (decision space, pre-verified)

A content-only clock nudge on the bargain branch, verified by the route-space
harness. Three single-edit variants were measured during this intake on scratch
copies of `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv` (tracked content untouched):

| Variant (one row's `clockCost`) | `gated beat` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| none (HEAD) | `routes=4 completed=0 clockLeft={2,2}` | baseline defect |
| `le-ii-bargain` 3 → 2 | `routes=10 completed=8 clockLeft={0,0}` | fixes 10 of 14 expiries; gated runs finish on 0 clock |
| `le-ii-sabotage` 2 → 1 | `routes=10 completed=8 clockLeft={0,0}` | same repair; last-tick finish on the cheap route preserved |
| `le-iii-approach` 3 → 2 | `routes=8 completed=6 clockLeft={0,2}` | touches every route; changes the shared Act III beat |
| `le-ii-bargain` 3 → 2 **and** `le-iii-ahead` 3 → 2 | `routes=10 completed=8 clockLeft={0,1}` | the only variant measured with **clock to spare** on a gated route: named route `gated-sabotage-core` → `closed` / `le-end-ram`, score 67, `clockLeft=1` |

Trade-off to weigh during implementation (recorded, not decided here): every
bargain-branch reduction lowers the "exactly zero clock" *last tick* finish that
the observation log calls the spike's best dramatic moment (the `first`-policy
route currently ends with `clock 0`). Making `le-ii-sabotage` itself cheaper
(variant 3) repairs the gated branch **without** touching that moment, but leaves
the gated runs finishing on 0 clock rather than with spare. A `DEFAULT_CLOCK_MAX`
bump (17 → 18) also works and is explicitly permitted, but it lengthens every run
and still lands gated runs on 0 clock, so it is the least targeted lever.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least one route through `le-ii-sabotage` reaches an ending (`reset`, `quiet`
  or `ram`) without expiring, proven by `npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts
  --seeds 40` reporting `gated beat: routes=… completed >= 1` (baseline
  `completed=0`).
- The clock left on the surviving gated route(s) is recorded in this work item;
  the intended outcome is at least one such route finishing with **≥ 1 clock
  unspent** (the "with clock to spare" reading of the source finding), and the
  chosen nudge is justified against that target.
- The branch's promise matches delivery: the scene help panel's "Pressure clock
  and state gates" slide and its Test Plan describe the gated branch as an earned
  *and completable* path — or the promotion of the branch is removed.
- No regression to the rest of the content: all four endings remain reachable
  (`le-end-reset`, `le-end-quiet`, `le-end-ram`, `le-end-abandon`), a cheap route
  still reaches the Loom's core and the reset ending, and the goodwill gate still
  opens at exactly 3 (`tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`,
  `tests/gym/LongErasureContent.test.ts`).
- The fix is content-only (CSV `clockCost` values and/or scene help text) **or** an
  explicitly justified `DEFAULT_CLOCK_MAX` change; no change to
  `src/story-line/**` engine behaviour, and no new `#when` / gate semantics.
- A regression test fails on the pre-fix content and passes on the fixed content —
  e.g. extend `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts` to walk the documented gated
  route to an ending and assert `status: 'complete'`, a non-`expired` outcome and
  the remaining clock. (Promoting the playtest harness into an authored-content CI
  guard is explicitly **out of scope** — see Related work.)
- `npm run storylines:validate` and `npm run storylines:graph -- --check` are
  clean (the committed manifest `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-manifest.json`
  is regenerated when content changes), and `tests/gym/**` plus the scene browser
  test stay green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who earns the secret `Sabotage the Loom` path can now finish the voyage
and reach an ending with clock in hand, instead of being the only player the clock
silently deletes.

## Constraints

- **Content-only.** This is a content-balance defect; the engine's clock, gate and
  affordability semantics must not change (`GymLongErasureGame.ts` stays
  Phaser-free and behaviourally identical apart from a justified
  `DEFAULT_CLOCK_MAX` value).
- **Mechanics-baseline fixture.** `tests/fixtures/story-line/prose/long-erasure-mechanics-baseline.json`
  is a prose-rewrite guard asserting that a *later* rewrite changed no mechanics;
  `tests/gym/LongErasureProse.test.ts` compares against it. Any `clockCost` change
  must update that fixture **and** the work item must record why (this item is the
  authorised mechanics change; the baseline is re-frozen from the fixed content).
- **Existing expiry fixtures.** `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`'s
  `EXPIRY_PATH` asserts a specific 19-clock route expires at `le-iii-approach`.
  The chosen nudge must either keep that route expiring (it still does with
  `le-ii-bargain` 3 → 2 or `le-ii-sabotage` 2 → 1) or the fixture path is replaced
  with an equivalently slow route and the replacement noted.
- **Verbatim doc quotes.** `tests/tooling/story-line-prose-docs.test.ts` requires
  every CSV block quoted in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  to appear verbatim in shipped content. The quoted row is `le-i-open` (plus the
  `le-ii-sabotage` options cell at `story-line.md:303`), so changing
  `le-ii-bargain` / `le-ii-sabotage` / `le-iii-*` clock costs must keep those
  quoted rows byte-identical, or the doc quote must be updated with the content.
- **Clock escalation test.** `tests/gym/LongErasureContent.test.ts` asserts
  `maxClock('II') >= maxClock('I')` and `maxClock('III') >= maxClock('I')`; with
  `le-ii-keep` still at 3 the Act II maximum survives any bargain-branch nudge.
- **Historical log.** `docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md` is dated measured

# 1. Baseline (expect completed=0)
npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts --seeds 40

# 2. After the content nudge (expect completed >= 1, clock reported)
npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts --seeds 40

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the Gym spike is retained as a playable demonstrator.** The source
  finding's own caveat is "fix it here only if the Gym spike is kept as a playable
  demonstrator"; it is (registered in `GymRegistry`, covered by
  `GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` / `GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts`,
  documented in `GYM_INDEX.md` and the Gym README), and the GDD

  chain as a scene's body — so the fix is not wasted work under either outcome.
- **Assumption — "with clock to spare" means ≥ 1 unspent clock on at least one
  surviving gated route**, while the hard pass condition is `completed >= 1` (the
  proof the source finding names). Both are reported, so a producer who reads the
  phrase strictly can see the number rather than infer it.
- **Risk — last-tick drama.** A clock nudge that fixes the branch also makes the
  cheapest route finish with more than 0 clock, weakening the "you spent your final
  tick on the weave" moment the observation log singles out. Mitigation: prefer the
  most targeted lever (`le-ii-sabotage` or `le-ii-bargain`), and note in the item
  whichever moment is preserved.
- **Risk — fixture churn.** `EXPIRY_PATH`, the mechanics baseline, the manifest and
  the prose-doc verbatim quotes all encode today's numbers; a careless edit reddens
  several suites at once. Mitigation: change one `clockCost` at a time and re-run
  the harness, then run `/skill:test --type unit`.
- **Risk — re-baselining hides a regression.** Re-freezing the mechanics baseline
  fixture is legitimate only for the authorised clock change; the fixture's `note`
  must be updated to say which values changed and why.
- **Risk — the gated branch becomes *too* easy.** Making the goodwill path cheaper
  than the cheap path would invert the design intent (it is meant to be the slow,
  earned route). Mitigation: keep route length unchanged and verify the cheap
  route's score/last-tick behaviour is not overtaken by the gated route.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Discoverability, affordability surfacing, epilogue arc
  credit and CI-guard promotion are recorded as linked work, not absorbed here.

- Surface affordability ("2 charge needed") instead of hiding gated options.
- Branch discoverability (1 of 160 policy runs ever saw `Sabotage the Loom`).
- Promote the route-space enumeration into a CI guard asserting every gated branch
  has a surviving route and every ending is reachable.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: every open point was resolvable from the
repository, the observation log and the committed harness. The interpretive
decisions are recorded below as assumptions for producer awareness (they may be
overridden without re-running intake).

- **Q1 — Is the Gym spike still a playable demonstrator, so this should be fixed
  rather than parked?** Answer (intake, from repository evidence): **yes**.
  Evidence: `GymRegistry.ts` registers `GymLongErasureScene`; the scene has a
  dedicated browser test and a smoke-test slot; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` and
  `example-games/gym/README.md` document it as a shipped Gym scene; the GDD
  `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` (status `open`, stage `idea`) recommends keeping the card
  chain as the body of a scene, so the content survives a C-hybrid too. Source:
  repo inspection, 2026-11-21. **Recommended:** fix here (this brief) — the defect
  is live in a shipped demonstrator today, not only under the GDD.
- **Q2 — What does "reaches an ending … with clock to spare" mean numerically?**
  Answer (intake interpretation): the hard pass condition is `gated beat:
  completed >= 1` (the proof the source finding names); the *target* is ≥ 1
  unspent clock on at least one surviving gated route, reported explicitly in the
  work item. Evidence: the source finding's parenthetical names only
  `completed >= 1`; the clock-left figure is reported separately by the harness
  (`gated beat: … clockLeftOnEntry`), so both readings are auditable.
  **Recommended:** implement to ≥ 1 unspent clock (achieved by the measured
  `le-ii-bargain` 3 → 2 + `le-iii-ahead` 3 → 2 combination) and record the number.
- **Q3 — Which lever: content clock nudge, cheaper Act III arrival, or
  `DEFAULT_CLOCK_MAX`?** Answer (intake recommendation, pre-verified): a
  **content clock nudge on the bargain branch**, preferring the most targeted
  single edit. Evidence: variant measurements in "Desired change" above — a single
  `clockCost` reduction (`le-ii-bargain` 3 → 2 or `le-ii-sabotage` 2 → 1) lifts

## Summary

Extend the authored-content route-space guard with a **scene-space mode** (`storylines:guard --manifest <file>`) that enumerates scene exits and beat refusals, and asserts two invariants: no exhausted close classifies as `success`, and no refusal leads to a state with no reachable ending.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.4 third static check (the clock is not a declared resource, so the content guard cannot see it).
- §2.8.6 item 5 (prove no scene exit strands the player) and §2.8 hull row (hull-costing doors stay survivable).
- §2.10 T3/T5 pacing evidence: a refusal or a hidden gate must never strand or silently truncate a run.
- §5.2 scene-space guard (named build-epic check).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` enumerates the playable route space of the **card chain** over declared resources (`gated-branch-survivable`, `ending-reachable`, `consequential-rejoin`).
- It has no manifest input, no scene boundary, no clock and no outcome/route semantics; the clock is not a declared resource, so a budget exhaustion is invisible to it.
- Bounds and clamping (G4) do not exist either, so a loss that clamps would currently enumerate differently from the authored intent.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Medium** (2-5 days): the nearest precedent is `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` itself (955 lines of bounded DFS with fail-closed truncation reporting) — this entry extends its state model with scene/clock/outcome, reusing its bound and reporting machinery.
- Band is medium because the enumeration machinery exists; the new work is state shape and the two invariants.

## Proposed shape

- Add a `--manifest` mode to `scripts/storyline-guard.ts`; keep the existing CSV mode unchanged.
- Enumerate (scene, beat, clock remaining, resources, outcome rules applied) states with the existing depth/state bounds; a bound hit stays a failure.
- Report per invariant, per scene exit and per refusal, in the existing JSON shape.
- Positive control required: a fixture whose exhausted close classifies `success` and a fixture whose refusal strands the player must both fail.

## Summary

Give the declared resource set **bounds**: per-key min/max, spill at the maximum, clamped loss at the minimum, and a reported remainder. Deltas are applied through the declared projection, so every game with more than the `coins` / `reputation` pair gets the same guarantee.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 resource model: the ranges table (`hull` 0-5, `morale` 0-8, `stores` 0-6, `goodwill` 0-5, `charge` 1-2), the "surplus spills, loss clamps" behaviour and the failure state per key.
- §2.10 tension design (a clamped loss at zero must be recorded, not silently ignored).
- §2.8.6 item 1 (bounds and clamping are named gaps) and item 2 (bounds become manifest data, owned with G2).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `createResourceProjection(...).applyResourceDelta` in `src/story-line/resources.ts` forwards every finite, non-zero delta to the game's field mutator with no bounds: a gain past a cap banks, a loss below zero goes negative, and nothing is reported.
- `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` (same module) is a value bag, not a bounds declaration.
- The nearest constrained-resource helper, `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, is hard-coded to `coins` / `reputation` and exposes only `minCoins` / `minReputation` (no maximum, no spill, no clamped-loss record).

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small-medium** (1-3 days): the nearest precedent is `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts` (constraint-checked deltas) and the `StorylineResourceProjection` seam in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small-medium because the seam and its tests exist; the work is a bounds type, clamp/spill arithmetic, a reported remainder and propagation through the GDD's manifest data (G2).

## Proposed shape

- `StorylineResourceBounds = Readonly<Record<key, { min: number; max: number }>>`.
- `applyResourceDelta` returns (or reports through a callback) `{ applied, spilled, clamped }` per key; never silently discards.
- Absent bounds keep today's unbounded behaviour, so no existing game changes.
- Unit tests: spill at max, clamp at min, multi-key delta ordering, absent bounds backward compatibility.

## Summary

Make **irreversibility** an engine guarantee: a declared irreversible resource key can never be granted by an option `#extra` or a manifest loss rule, and the refusal is a hard authoring error, not an authoring convention.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 `hull` as the irreversible tension dial (0-5, no recovery within a run).
- §2.10 irreversible-loss tension and the reset ending's structural recovery.
- §2.8.6 item 6 (`#extra=hull:1` is legal content today).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `resources.irreversible` is manifest data read only by the proposed manifest validator rule `loss-not-irreversible` (GDD §2.4); the manifest validator itself does not exist (G2).
- Nothing in `src/story-line/resources.ts` knows the concept: `selectDeclaredDelta` filters undeclared keys only (`ignored`), so a grant to a declared irreversible key is applied.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` refuses `unknown-resource-key` (a key outside the declared set) but cannot refuse a *direction* on a declared key.
- The GDD's guard is a fixture test plus authoring discipline (GDD §2.8.3/§2.8.6), which is the gap this entry closes.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the `unknown-resource-key` rule in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` (a declarative, row + column + reason diagnostic) plus the `selectDeclaredDelta` sign handling in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one declaration, one validation rule and one guard in the projection.

## Proposed shape

- Declare irreversible keys alongside the declared set (`StorylineResourceProjection` option or manifest data).
- Reject a positive delta to an irreversible key at authoring time (validator code, e.g. `irreversible-grant`) and at resolution time (refuse, log).
- Unit tests: a `#extra=hull:1` row fails validation with the row/column reason; a negative hull cost still applies.

## Summary

**Surface affordability** instead of deleting it: compile an unaffordable option into a requirement object (which keys, how much is needed, how much the player has) so a presenting layer can render it disabled with its shortfall, rather than omitting it at draw time.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.3/§2.9 "an unaffordable option is not shown" — the presentation contract must say why.
- §2.8.6 item 3 (measured cost: 32 of 302 option instances hidden; 107 of 197 dead turns gate-collapsed).
- §3.6 B4 affordability presentation; §2.10 T5 (hidden affordability is not tension).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `isOptionAffordable(option, resources, declaredResources)` in `src/story-line/compile.ts` returns a boolean.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` filters unaffordable options out of `compiledOptions` at draw time, so the presenting layer never sees them; there is no requirement/shortfall shape anywhere in the compiled option model.
- `StorylineOption` (in `src/story-line/types.ts`) carries the `cost` declaration but no computed affordability state.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is `isOptionAffordable` itself plus the compiled-option shape in `src/story-line/compile.ts`; the arithmetic exists, only the output shape changes.
- Band is small because it is an additive field on the compiled option and a policy switch (omit vs surface), with no new evaluator.

## Proposed shape

- `OptionAffordability = { affordable: true } | { affordable: false; shortfall: Array<{ key; required; available }> }`.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` gains a policy option (`'omit'` default, preserving every current caller and test; `'surface'` keeps the option with its affordability state).
- Resolution still refuses an unaffordable option (unchanged), so surfacing cannot create an illegal play path.
- Unit tests: default policy unchanged; surface policy yields the shortfall per key; an unaffordable surfaced option cannot resolve.

Run the human browser playtest the GDD recommends (ideally three people, at least one who has not read the content) over the v1 Long Erasure content, and record measured wall-clock run durations, phone-screen readability and felt tension.

## Why

The v1 scope statement (CG-0MWPY2HJU006LJMU, GDD §7.2) estimates playtime at 13 minutes a run (10–16 range) from the measured beats-per-run figure (spike: 6–10 beats, mean 8.48) multiplied by two stated, unmeasured assumptions: 35–50 s a beat (A1) and ~3 min presentation overhead (A2). This playtest is the measurement that replaces A1 and A2. It also closes the evidence limit recorded in GDD §2.6 (agent-driven structural measurement, not felt enjoyment) and lifts deferral D3 of the GDD's deferred list (§7.6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Three participants (at least one who has not read the content) each play at least one complete run in a browser, with wall-clock duration recorded from opening to epilogue.
- The measured durations are compared with the 10–16 minute range and the 13-minute target; the difference and its cause are recorded.

gates play exactly as authored — with no TypeScript edit and no second card
catalogue to keep in step.

`GymStorylineScene` renders `DEMO_CARDS`, a hard-coded catalogue in
`example-games/gym/GymStorylineDemo.ts`. Nothing in the scene's runtime path
reads the CSV (`createSceneRuntime()` -> `createDemoRuntime()` -> `DEMO_CARDS`;
no `fetch`, no `?raw` import, no CSV parse). Consequences:

- Editor edits to `storylines.csv` never reach the Gym scene — observed
  2026-11-22: the author renamed `gym-story-start` to "Town Roads", rewrote its
  `context` and `effect`, regenerated the manifest/Mermaid, restarted the dev
  server, and saw no change in the demo.
- The catalogue and the CSV are kept in sync only by a test assertion
  (`tests/gym/GymStorylineContent.test.ts` -> "carries the same card ids,
  context and authored outcomes as the CSV"), so a content edit leaves the
  suite red until a developer copies the prose across by hand.
- The two copies have already diverged mechanically: the CSV's `Invest` option
  carries `#cost=coins:5#extra=reputation:+2#when=coins>=100>gym-story-end`,
  while `DEMO_CARDS` carries only `#says`. The parity test does not compare
  option mechanics, so the played demo is not mechanically the authored

shape: it imports its CSV via `?raw` and builds content with
`longErasureContentFromCsv()` (`src/story-line/content/csv.ts`).

## Summary

Implement §2.3 step A: entering a beat charges its `clockCost` against the scene's remaining clock, presents it, and refuses a beat that cannot be afforded — closing the scene with `budget-exhausted` before any option is presented.

## Scope

- `enterBeat(cardId)` on the runner: refusal check, charge, and a returned entry record (`cardId`, `clockCost`, `clockRemaining`) so the caller can render the card's `context` prose and the scene banner.
- `budgetExhausted` flag set by a refusal and carried into the scene close.
- The options the caller presents come from `storyline.getStorylineOptions` gated by `isOptionAffordable` — the runner does not filter or re-derive affordability itself.
- A requested entry that is already unaffordable drives the close path handed to the next feature (scene close), not a partial entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Beat entry matches §2.3 step A: an affordable beat is charged and presented, and the entry record reports the charged cost and the post-charge `clockRemaining`.
- A beat whose cost exactly equals the remaining clock is affordable, leaves `clockRemaining` at 0, and is reported as presented (spending the last tick is legal).
- A beat whose `clockCost` exceeds the remaining clock is refused, never played, its options are never presented, and it closes the scene with `budgetExhausted = true` and reason `budget-exhausted`.
- One test per clause above, registered against the §2.3 step map entry for A.2 / A.3.
- Beat entry consumes no RNG: the adapter double's RNG call count is unchanged across an affordable entry and across a refusal.
- The "Episode runner → Beat entry" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the refusal rule and the exact-cost clause.

## Minimal Implementation

- `enterBeat` reads `Beat.clockCost` from the validated manifest, compares against `sceneClockRemaining`, charges or refuses, and returns an immutable entry record.
- Refusal sets `budgetExhausted` on the run state and reports reason `budget-exhausted`; presenting options stays the caller's step.
- Three tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-beat-entry.test.ts` (affordable, exact-cost, refused) plus one RNG-accounting test.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 step B: the player's option resolves through `@story-line` unchanged, and the runner classifies the pushed card into "continue the scene" or "close the scene with this pending chain" — the boundary rule that makes the beat set the scene boundary.

## Scope

- `resolveChoice(option)` on the runner: delegate to `storyline.resolveStorylineOption`, then classify `pushedCard`.
- Classification: in-scene beat → continue at that beat; out-of-scene beat → close with `pendingChain = pushedCard`; ending card → close with `pendingChain = pushedCard`; no pushed card → close with `pendingChain = null`.
- The runner never re-reads an `options` cell, re-implements successor precedence or keeps a second declared key set (constraint: one choice model).
- The returned classification record names the case and the pending chain so the scene close and the tests read one shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Choice resolution delegates to `storyline.resolveStorylineOption` for every case, asserted with a spy on the storyline double — the runner contains no second resolution path.
- An in-scene pushed card continues the scene: the runner reports `next: "continue"` and leaves the run state inside the same scene.
- An out-of-scene pushed card closes the scene with `pendingChain` set to that card id and `next: "close"`.
- An ending card pushed by a choice closes the scene with `pendingChain` set to the ending card id and `next: "close"`.
- A resolution that pushes no card closes the scene with `pendingChain = null` and `next: "close"`.
- One test per `pushedCard` case (in-scene beat, out-of-scene beat, ending card, none), registered against the §2.3 step map B.5 entries.

## Minimal Implementation

- `resolveChoice` calls `storyline.resolveStorylineOption(state, card, option)`, then a pure `classifyPushedCard` helper reading the manifest's assigned-card index and `manifest.endings`.
- The classification is a discriminated union (`continue` / `close`) with `pendingChain` set only on the close cases.
- Four tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-choice.test.ts`, each naming its case.

## Dependencies

- Depends on beat entry (`Episode runner beat entry: clock charge and refusal`) — a choice is always made from an entered beat.

## Summary

Implement the loss ledger of §2.2.8: chain losses observed by diffing `engine.getResources` across a beat resolution, and rule losses applied at scene close — both recorded with the GDD's field names, never as a positive line, and never as arithmetic of the runner's own.

## Scope

- Chain-loss diffing: snapshot the irreversible keys before a choice resolves, diff after, and record one `{ kind: "chain", sceneId, beatId, field, delta }` per negative net change.
- Rule-loss recording seam used by scene close: `{ kind: "rule", sceneId, ruleId, field, delta, statement }` appended in declaration order.
- The ledger is read-only to callers (`getLossLedger()`), ordered by observation, JSON-safe.
- The runner performs no resource arithmetic: every observed delta is what `engine.applyResourceDelta` applied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The loss ledger records chain entries for negative net irreversible deltas observed across a beat resolution, carrying the GDD's field names (`kind`, `sceneId`, `beatId`, `field`, `delta`).
- A net positive (refund) change on an irreversible key records nothing — the ledger never contains a positive `delta` line.
- A fired loss rule records a rule entry (`kind: "rule"`, `sceneId`, `ruleId`, `field`, `delta`, `statement`) in declaration order.
- Ledger lines are appended in observation order and exposed read-only; mutating the returned array does not change runner state.
- No loss line is recorded unless a corresponding `engine.applyResourceDelta` call was made (asserted against the adapter double's delta recorder).
- The ledger survives a JSON round-trip unchanged (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(lines))` deep-equals the original).

## Minimal Implementation

- A `lossLedger` array in run state plus an internal `recordChainLoss` / `recordRuleLoss` pair; both are pure appends.
- The chain diff wraps the choice resolution: read the irreversible-key subset of `engine.getResources`, resolve, read again, record negatives.
- Tests in `tests/story-line/episode-runner-loss-ledger.test.ts` using a card that applies an irreversible cost and one that grants a refund.

## Summary

Implement §2.3 steps C.6–C.8: evaluate the scene objective once against post-resolution resources, classify the outcome first-match-wins from the authored rules (including an authored `budget: "exhausted"` rule), and apply every matching loss rule through the engine seam.

## Scope

- Objective evaluation: `check` against `engine.getResources` after the resolving choice, absent keys reading 0, recorded as `objectiveMet`.
- Outcome classification: first matching `outcomeRule` in declaration order over `{ objective }`, `{ budget }` and raw `{ field, op, value }` conditions; the catch-all guarantees totality (no defensive fallback in code).
- Loss-rule application: every matching `losses` rule in declaration order through `engine.applyResourceDelta`, one ledger rule line and one `engine.appendLog` line per rule (statement plus signed amount and key).
- `budgetExhausted` is classified by the authored table, never hard-coded to `failure`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scene close matches §2.3 steps C.6–C.9: the objective is evaluated exactly once, against post-resolution resources; classification is first-match-wins in declaration order and honours an authored `{ budget: "exhausted" }` rule placed before the catch-all; every matching loss rule is applied through `engine.applyResourceDelta` in declaration order, producing one ledger line and one activity-log line each.
- Classification is first-match-wins in declaration order and honours an authored `{ budget: "exhausted" }` rule placed before the catch-all, so a refused close in `s-iii-core` classifies `failure` through `watch-spent`.
- Every matching loss rule is applied through `engine.applyResourceDelta` in declaration order, producing one ledger rule line and one activity-log line each (statement plus signed amount and key).

## Summary

Implement §2.3 steps C.9–C.12: select the first matching route in declaration order, resolve its `chain` / `beat` / `ending` target, emit the nine-field `scene-exit` record, and enter the target scene with a fresh clock, an appended history entry and irreversible keys untouched.

## Scope

- Route selection: first route where `on` matches (`*` or the outcome) **and** `when` is absent-or-matching **and** the route is not a `chain` route while `pendingChain` is null.
- Target resolution: `chain` → the pending chain card; `beat` with explicit `beat` → that card; `beat` without → the target scene's `entryBeat`; `ending` → present the ending card and close the run.
- `scene-exit` emission: exactly `{ sceneId, objectiveMet, outcome, ruleId, routeId, clockSpent, clockRemaining, budgetExhausted, nextBeat }`, appended once per close in close order.
- Scene entry: reset the clock to the target scene's `budget.clock`, push the scene id onto `sceneHistory` (route id onto `routeHistory`), clear `pendingChain`, leave every irreversible key unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Routing matches §2.3 steps C.9–C.12: the first matching route in declaration order wins, honouring `on` and `when`; a `chain` route is skipped when `pendingChain` is null.
- `chain`, `beat` (with and without an explicit `beat`) and `ending` targets each resolve correctly, with a `beat` target without a beat opening the target scene's `entryBeat`.
- Entering a scene resets `sceneClockRemaining` to its `budget.clock`, pushes the scene id onto `sceneHistory` (and the route id onto `routeHistory`), clears `pendingChain`, and leaves irreversible resource keys unchanged.
- The `scene-exit` record carries exactly the nine fields of §2.3 step 11 and is the single source the journal/banner data is derived from; it is appended once per scene close and never rewritten.
- An `ending` target presents the ending card and closes the run, and the reset ending's restart action returns the run to `start`.
- Route selection, scene entry and `scene-exit` emission consume no RNG (adapter RNG call count unchanged across a full scripted scene close).

- `selectRoute(outcome, context)`, `resolveRouteTarget(target)`, `emitSceneExit(...)` and `enterScene(sceneId, beatId)` as pure-ish helpers on the runner; the run state is the only mutation target.

## Summary

Prove and pin determinism: the runner consumes no RNG outside the seeded `@story-line` candidate draw, and two runs at the same seed with the same choice sequence produce identical scene exits, ledger lines and final outcome.

## Scope

- An RNG-accounting test across a full scripted run: every draw is attributable to option resolution, none to entry, close, classification, loss application or routing.
- A same-seed/same-choices comparison over two independently constructed runners producing identical ordered `scene-exit` records, ledger lines and final outcome.
- A source-scan test asserting no `Math.random` occurrence in the runner module.
- A table-order sensitivity test documenting that reordering a route table is the only lever that changes a decision at a fixed seed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Determinism is proven by test: two runs with the same seed and the same choice sequence produce identical ordered `scene-exit` records, identical ledger lines and the same final outcome.
- No RNG is consumed by beat entry, scene close, outcome classification, loss application or routing — asserted by an RNG-call ledger that attributes every draw to an option resolution.
- `Math.random` does not appear in `src/story-line/episode-runner.ts` (source-scan test), and no `Date.now()` / timestamp enters the scene-exit record or the ledger.
- Reordering two competing routes in an in-memory manifest copy flips the decision — the only lever at a fixed seed — while an unmodified copy reproduces byte-identical records after JSON serialisation.
- The "Determinism" subsection in `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` states the one-RNG rule and links the tests that pin it.

- `tests/story-line/episode-runner-determinism.test.ts` with a double that records every `rng(state)` call tagged with the pipeline stage the runner reports.
